simple.meaning: חָשָׁה (châshâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to hush or keep quiet.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 16 times across Judges, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, Nehemiah, Psalms, and 2 more, beginning at Judges 18:9. Its contexts include family line, kingship, prophetic witness, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָשָׁה (H2814).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חָשָׁה (châshâh) / H2814 is traced through Judges 18:9, 1 Kings 22:3, 2 Kings 2:3, 2 Kings 2:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: They said, “Arise, and let’s go up against them; for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good. Do you stand still? Don’t be slothful to go and to enter in to possess the land.
The king of Israel said to his servants, “You know that Ramoth Gilead is ours, and we do nothing, and don’t take it out of the hand of the king of Syria?”
The sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha, and said to him, “Do you know that Yahweh will take away your master from your head today?”
The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho came near to Elisha, and said to him, “Do you know that Yahweh will take away your master from your head today?”

Then they said to one another, “We aren’t doing right. Today is a day of good news, and we keep silent. If we wait until the morning light, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore come, let’s go and tell the king’s household.”
So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Hold your peace, for the day is holy. Don’t be grieved.”
My heart was hot within me.
He makes the storm a calm,
“I have been silent a long time.
For Zion’s sake I will not hold my peace,
I have set watchmen on your walls, Jerusalem.
Our holy and our beautiful house where our fathers praised you

definitions.usage: hold peace, keep silence, be silent, (be) still.
definitions.full: H2814. chashah [ חָשָׁה ] verb be silent, inactive, still (chiefly in poetry and late) (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic in derivatives) — Qal Imperfect 2masculine singular תֶּחֱשֶׁה Psa 28:1 ; Isa 64:11 ; אֶחֱשֶׁה 62:1 ; 65:6 ; יֶחֱשׁוּ 62:6 ; וַיֶּחֱשׁוּ Psa 107:29 ; — be silent Eccl 3:7 (opposed to לְדַבֵּר ); Isa 62:1 , 6 (= neglect to speak); of ׳י i.e. be unresponsive Psa 28:1 (|| חרשׁ ); Isa 64:11 (|| הִתְאַמַּק ); but 65:6 of ׳י 's keeping silence at iniquity, i.e. overlooking it (compare 57:11 Hiph`il); of waves, be still Psa 107:29 (subject גַּלֵּיהֶם ). Hiph`il Perfect הֶחֱשֵׁיתִי Psa 39:3 ; Isa 42:14 ; Imperative הֶחֱשׁוּ 2Kin 2:3 , 5 ; Participle מַחְשֶׁה Isa 57:11 ; plural מַחְשִׁים Judg 18:9 3 t.; — 1 exhibit silence, be silent 2Kin 2:3 , 5 ; 7:9 ; Psa 39:3 (followed by מִטּוֺב , || נֶאֱלַמְתִּי ), figurative Isa 42:14 (|| אחרישׁ ); of ׳י 's being silent at iniquity 57:11 (i.e. overlooking it, compare Qal 65:5 ), possibly also is be silent , opposed to rescue , Ges Che Di Du. 2 shew inactivity Judg 18:9 , ׳הח מִקַּחַת 1Kin 22:3 Gilead is ours, and we shew inactivity so as not to take it . 3 causat . make still, quiet , followed by לְ , of direct object Neh 8:11 (v:b הַסּוּ q. v.) חֻשָם חֻשִׁים, see above.
